id.description:
Unique identifier for the content being reported in moderation workflows. Uses UUID v4 format for global uniqueness and security.

This identifier links back to the original content entity (post, comment, or member profile) that is subject to moderation review.
The ID ensures precise content targeting and prevents ambiguity in moderation actions.

type.description:
Type of content being reported, categorizing the moderation target for workflow routing.

Supported values include 'post' for discussion board posts, 'comment' for threaded comments, and 'member_profile' for user profile content.
This classification enables efficient moderation queue assignment and specialized handling procedures based on content category.

title.description:
Title or summary description of the content being reported, providing essential context for moderation decisions.

For posts, this represents the post title; for comments, a summary of the comment content; for profiles, the member's display name.
This field enables moderators to quickly assess content context without needing to access the full content body during initial review.

IDiscussionBoardPost.ISummary.description:
Summary view of content for moderation reporting and reference purposes.

Provides essential identification and context for content being reported in moderation workflows, optimized for efficient display in moderation interfaces while maintaining complete content context.

This summary DTO enables rapid content identification and categorization during moderation queue processing, supporting quick decision-making while preserving audit trail integrity.

Used primarily in content report creation and moderation dashboard displays where full content details are not immediately required but basic identification is essential for workflow management.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the configuration setting.

Unique identifier automatically generated by the system to ensure each configuration setting has a distinct identity. Used for internal reference and relationship management within the database.

config_key.description:
Unique identifier key for the configuration setting.

This key serves as the human-readable identifier for the configuration setting (e.g., 'max_attachment_size', 'post_moderation_enabled'). Each key must be unique across the entire configuration system to prevent conflicts and ensure consistent behavior.

The key follows a naming convention that describes the setting's purpose and scope, making it easily identifiable by administrators and developers.

config_value.description:
Value associated with the configuration key.

Stores the actual setting value as a string for maximum flexibility. The interpretation of this value depends on the config_type field, which specifies how the value should be processed (boolean, number, string, json).

For boolean values, this field should contain 'true' or 'false'. For numeric values, it should contain the number as a string. For JSON values, it should contain valid JSON syntax.

config_type.description:
Data type specification for the configuration value.

Indicates how the config_value field should be interpreted and processed. Valid types include:
- 'boolean': True/false values
- 'number': Numeric values
- 'string': Text values
- 'json': Complex structured data

This field ensures proper type validation and prevents type mismatches when configuration values are used throughout the system.

description.description:
Human-readable description of the configuration setting.

Provides context and documentation about the purpose, usage, and impact of this configuration setting. This description helps administrators understand what the setting controls and how changes might affect system behavior.

Should be clear, concise, and informative to support effective configuration management.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was created.

Records the exact date and time when this configuration setting was first added to the system. This audit trail helps track configuration changes and understand the evolution of system settings over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was last modified.

Tracks the most recent modification to this configuration setting. This field is automatically updated whenever changes are made, providing a complete history of configuration modifications for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.description:
Discussion board configuration entity representing system-wide settings and parameters.

This entity stores platform configuration settings that control various aspects of the discussion board system behavior, including moderation policies, attachment limits, content guidelines, and system customization options. Each configuration has a unique key-value pair with type specification and descriptive documentation.

Configuration settings are managed by authorized administrators and moderators who can create, update, and maintain system parameters without requiring code changes. The system uses these configurations to dynamically adjust behavior based on organizational needs and platform requirements.

Security considerations include access controls to prevent unauthorized modification of critical system settings. Configuration changes can significantly impact platform stability and user experience, so modification privileges are restricted to trusted administrative roles.

page.description:
Page number for paginated configuration results retrieval.

Specifies which page of configuration settings to retrieve, starting from page 1. Each page contains a configurable number of configuration records based on the limit parameter.

Used in conjunction with limit to implement efficient pagination for browsing large configuration sets. The system automatically calculates total pages based on record count and page size.

limit.description:
Maximum number of configuration records to return per page.

Controls the page size for configuration listing operations. The system enforces a maximum limit of 100 records per page to prevent excessive resource consumption and ensure optimal performance.

Smaller limits improve response times for clients that don't require the full configuration set at once, while larger limits reduce the number of API calls needed for complete configuration retrieval.

search.description:
Search term for filtering configurations by key patterns or description content.

Performs case-insensitive pattern matching across configuration keys and descriptions. Useful for quickly locating specific settings among potentially hundreds of system configurations.

Supports partial matching, allowing administrators to find configurations using keywords or phrases without needing exact key names.

config_type_filter.description:
Filter to restrict results to configurations of a specific data type.

Valid options include 'boolean', 'number', 'string', and 'json'. This parameter helps administrators focus on configurations that share similar value types and processing requirements.

When omitted, configurations of all types are included in the results, providing a comprehensive view of all system settings.

oneOf.description:
Sort configurations alphabetically by their unique identifier keys.

Useful for organizing configurations in a predictable alphabetical order, making it easier to locate specific settings by their key names.

Sort configurations by their creation timestamp, showing newest configurations first.

Helps administrators identify recently added configuration settings and track the evolution of system parameters over time.

Sort configurations by their last modification timestamp, showing most recently updated settings first.

Useful for identifying configurations that have been recently changed, which may require additional review or testing.

order_by.description:
Field selection for sorting configuration search results.

Determines the primary sorting criteria for returned configurations. Available options include alphabetical sorting by configuration key or chronological sorting by creation or modification dates.

This parameter helps organize configuration listings in a meaningful way that supports efficient administrative review and management workflows.

oneOf.description:
Sort configurations in ascending order.

For alphabetical sorting, this means A-Z order. For date sorting, this means oldest to newest.

Useful for chronological analysis or when a specific ordering sequence is required.

Sort configurations in descending order.

For alphabetical sorting, this means Z-A order. For date sorting, this means newest to oldest.

Typically used with date fields to show most recent configurations first, which is often the most relevant view for administrative tasks.

order_direction.description:
Direction specification for configuration sorting.

Determines whether configurations are sorted in ascending (A-Z, oldest-first) or descending (Z-A, newest-first) order.

When combined with order_by, this parameter provides flexible sorting capabilities that can be tailored to specific administrative needs and workflows.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving discussion board configuration settings.

This request DTO provides comprehensive search capabilities for configuration management operations, allowing administrators to filter, sort, and paginate system configuration settings efficiently.

Supported filtering options include keyword search across configuration keys and descriptions, type-based filtering for specific data types, and flexible sorting by key, creation date, or modification date.

Pagination parameters ensure that large configuration sets can be managed effectively without overwhelming clients or servers. All parameters are optional, allowing clients to request configurations with varying levels of specificity based on their current administrative needs.

The DTO integrates with the discussion_board_configurations table structure, supporting all available configuration fields while maintaining performance and security considerations appropriate for system administration operations.

config_key.description:
Unique identifier key for the new configuration setting.

Must be globally unique across all system configurations. Follows naming conventions that clearly describe the setting's purpose and scope (e.g., 'max_attachment_size', 'post_moderation_enabled', 'user_registration_enabled').

This key will be used throughout the system to reference and apply the configuration setting, so it should be descriptive yet concise for easy identification and management.

config_value.description:
Initial value for the configuration setting, stored as a string for maximum flexibility.

The interpretation of this value depends on the specified config_type:
- For 'boolean' type: Use 'true' or 'false'
- For 'number' type: Provide numeric value as string (e.g., '100', '3.14')
- For 'string' type: Provide text content directly
- For 'json' type: Provide valid JSON syntax

This flexible approach allows the system to handle various configuration types while maintaining a consistent storage format.

config_type.description:
Data type specification that determines how the config_value should be interpreted.

Valid options include 'boolean', 'number', 'string', and 'json'. This field ensures proper validation and processing of configuration values throughout the system.

The type specification prevents type mismatches and ensures that configuration values are used correctly in different parts of the application, maintaining system stability and predictable behavior.

description.description:
Comprehensive human-readable description explaining the configuration's purpose, usage, and impact.

Should clearly describe what system behavior this setting controls, how changes affect platform functionality, and any important considerations when modifying the value.

Provides essential context for administrators to make informed decisions about configuration changes and understand the potential consequences of modifications to system settings.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating new discussion board configuration settings.

This DTO contains all necessary information to establish a new system configuration parameter that controls various aspects of platform behavior, including moderation policies, attachment limits, content guidelines, and system customization options.

Each configuration requires a unique key identifier, appropriate value with type specification, and comprehensive description to support effective configuration management. The system validates configuration key uniqueness and value-type compatibility before creating the new setting.

Security considerations include restricting this operation to authorized administrators only, as configuration settings control critical system behavior that can significantly impact platform stability, security, and user experience. System-generated fields like id, created_at, and updated_at are automatically populated and should not be included in creation requests.

config_value.description:
Updated value for the configuration setting.

If provided, replaces the existing configuration value. Must conform to the existing config_type of the configuration setting. For boolean values, use 'true' or 'false'. For numeric values, provide the number as a string. For JSON values, provide valid JSON syntax.

The system validates that the new value is compatible with the configuration's data type. If config_type is also being updated, the validation will use the new type specification. This ensures data integrity and prevents type mismatches that could cause system instability.

config_type.description:
Updated data type specification for the configuration value.

If provided, changes how the config_value is interpreted. Valid options: 'boolean', 'number', 'string', 'json'. Changing the config_type may require corresponding changes to the config_value to ensure compatibility.

The system validates that the new config_type is supported and that the existing config_value can be converted to the new type if necessary. This prevents configuration errors and maintains system stability during configuration updates.

description.description:
Updated human-readable description of the configuration setting.

If provided, replaces the existing description. Should clearly explain the configuration's purpose, usage, and any important considerations for administrators.

The description should be comprehensive enough to help administrators understand the impact of configuration changes on system behavior. This documentation is crucial for effective configuration management and troubleshooting.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating existing discussion board configuration settings.

This DTO allows partial updates to configuration settings. Only the fields provided will be modified; omitted fields retain their current values. This enables flexible configuration management without requiring complete re-specification of all settings.

The config_key field is provided as a URL path parameter and MUST NOT be duplicated in the request body to prevent security vulnerabilities. System-generated fields like id, created_at, and updated_at are managed automatically and cannot be modified through this DTO.

Security considerations: This operation requires moderator privileges. The system validates that configuration keys exist and that updated values conform to the specified type (or new type if config_type is modified). Rate limiting should be implemented to prevent abuse of configuration modification capabilities.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the configuration setting.

Unique identifier automatically generated by the system to ensure each configuration setting has a distinct identity. Used for internal reference and relationship management within the database.

This UUID serves as the immutable identifier for the configuration record throughout its lifecycle, providing a stable reference point for audit trails and system integrations.

config_key.description:
Unique identifier key for the configuration setting.

This key serves as the human-readable identifier for the configuration setting (e.g., 'max_attachment_size', 'post_moderation_enabled'). Each key must be unique across the entire configuration system to prevent conflicts and ensure consistent behavior.

The key follows a naming convention that describes the setting's purpose and scope, making it easily identifiable by administrators and developers. This field is indexed for efficient lookup operations.

config_value.description:
Value associated with the configuration key.

Stores the actual setting value as a string for maximum flexibility. The interpretation of this value depends on the config_type field, which specifies how the value should be processed (boolean, number, string, json).

For boolean values, this field should contain 'true' or 'false'. For numeric values, it should contain the number as a string. For JSON values, it should contain valid JSON syntax. The system performs type validation when configurations are used.

config_type.description:
Data type specification for the configuration value.

Indicates how the config_value field should be interpreted and processed. Valid types include:
- 'boolean': True/false values
- 'number': Numeric values
- 'string': Text values
- 'json': Complex structured data

This field ensures proper type validation and prevents type mismatches when configuration values are used throughout the system. It maintains data integrity across configuration operations.

description.description:
Human-readable description of the configuration setting.

Provides context and documentation about the purpose, usage, and impact of this configuration setting. This description helps administrators understand what the setting controls and how changes might affect system behavior.

Should be clear, concise, and informative to support effective configuration management. This documentation is essential for maintaining configuration consistency across administrative changes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was created.

Records the exact date and time when this configuration setting was first added to the system. This audit trail helps track configuration changes and understand the evolution of system settings over time.

This field is automatically set when the configuration is created and provides historical context for configuration management and troubleshooting activities.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration setting was last modified.

Tracks the most recent modification to this configuration setting. This field is automatically updated whenever changes are made, providing a complete history of configuration modifications for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

The updated_at field helps administrators identify when configurations were last changed and track the configuration lifecycle for compliance and maintenance purposes.

IDiscussionBoardConfiguration.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of discussion board configuration settings.

Provides essential information about platform-wide configuration parameters that control system behavior, moderation policies, and content guidelines. These settings are managed by administrators and affect how the discussion board operates.

The summary includes all configuration fields to provide complete information for configuration management interfaces. This comprehensive representation ensures administrators have access to all necessary details when reviewing and managing system configurations.

Security considerations: Configuration summaries are accessible to authorized administrators and moderators. Sensitive configuration values should be handled appropriately based on the configuration's purpose and potential impact on system security.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Can be set to null to restore a deleted guest account. This is the only field that can be meaningfully updated for guest accounts.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for guest users allowing modification of guest account status.

This DTO allows updating the soft deletion status of guest accounts. The deleted_at field can be modified to manage guest account lifecycle - setting it to a timestamp marks the account as deleted, while setting it to null restores a previously deleted account.

System-managed fields like id, guest_token, created_at, and updated_at are excluded as they are managed automatically by the system or are immutable identifiers. The guest_token field serves as the permanent identifier and cannot be changed after creation.

This DTO provides the primary update functionality for guest management operations, focusing exclusively on account lifecycle management through the deleted_at field.

id.description: Primary Key.

guest_token.description: Unique anonymous identifier for guest tracking without authentication requirements.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of guest user accounts.

Provides essential information about anonymous users who can browse content without authentication. Guest accounts serve as temporary identifiers for users exploring the platform before committing to registration.

This summary includes the guest token and timestamps for tracking guest activity and managing guest-to-member transitions. It provides a lightweight representation suitable for list views and guest management interfaces while maintaining all relevant guest account information.

The summary excludes detailed guest session information to maintain efficiency in list operations. Guest accounts can be tracked through their unique guest_token identifier and lifecycle timestamps for effective guest management.

pagination.description: Pagination parameters for controlling result sets and page navigation

search.description:
Search term for filtering guest tokens by partial matching. Supports case-insensitive substring search for flexible guest account identification.

Empty or null values disable search filtering, allowing for broad guest account queries without text constraints.

created_after.description:
Filter guests created after this timestamp for chronological analysis of guest registration patterns.

Enables date-range queries to track guest account creation trends and platform growth metrics over specific time periods.

created_before.description:
Filter guests created before this timestamp, complementing created_after for precise date-range filtering.

Combined with created_after, enables bounded time period queries for comprehensive guest activity reporting and analytics.

oneOf.description: Sort by guest account creation timestamp for chronological ordering of results.
Sort by guest account last update timestamp for recent activity-based ordering.
Sort by guest token value for alphabetical or identifier-based ordering.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by, determining the primary ordering criteria for paginated guest lists.

Supported sorting fields include creation timestamp, update timestamp, and guest token for flexible result organization based on different use cases.

oneOf.description: Ascending sort order returning oldest records first based on the selected sort_by field.
Descending sort order returning newest records first based on the selected sort_by field.

order.description:
Sorting direction controlling whether results are returned in ascending or descending order.

Ascending order returns records from oldest to newest, while descending order returns from newest to oldest based on the sort_by field selection.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for discussion board guest account queries.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for administrative guest management operations. It supports pagination through a unified pagination object, text search for guest token matching, date-range filtering for temporal analysis, and flexible sorting options.

The combination of search parameters enables precise targeting of guest accounts based on creation patterns, identifier characteristics, and temporal attributes. Empty or null values for optional parameters disable the corresponding filters, allowing for broad queries when specific filtering is not required.

This schema integrates with guest search operations to deliver filtered, paginated results while maintaining consistent pagination patterns across the API. The design supports both simple paginated queries and complex multi-criteria searches for comprehensive guest management functionality.

pagination.description: Pagination parameters for controlling result sets and page navigation in member queries

search.description:
Search term for filtering members by username, email, or display name using partial matching.

Supports case-insensitive substring search across multiple member fields for comprehensive member discovery and management.

created_after.description: Filter members created after this timestamp for registration date range queries

created_before.description: Filter members created before this timestamp for bounded registration period analysis

filter.description:
Additional filtering options for member search operations beyond basic text search.

Provides date-range filtering capabilities to analyze member registration patterns and platform growth over specific time periods.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering discussion board member accounts.

Provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for member management operations throughout the discussion board platform. Supports pagination for efficient handling of large result sets and various filtering options to narrow down member searches based on different criteria.

This schema enables both simple member list retrieval and complex multi-criteria searches, supporting administrative functions like member analytics, account management, and platform growth tracking. The unified pagination pattern ensures consistency with other search operations in the system.

email.description: Member email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all members and serves as the primary contact method for notifications and account recovery. Email updates require re-verification to ensure account security.

password.description: Plain text password for member authentication. Password updates require current password verification and must meet security requirements including minimum length, complexity, and uniqueness constraints. The backend will hash this password before storage.

display_name.description: Optional display name for member profile customization. Provides personalization while maintaining username uniqueness for system operations. Display names can be changed freely without affecting authentication credentials.

bio.description: Optional biography or description for member profile. Allows members to share information about themselves with the community. Bio content is subject to community guidelines and moderation policies.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate.description:
Update data for modifying member profile information.

This DTO contains fields that can be updated by authenticated members for their own profiles. It excludes immutable fields like id, username, created_at, and system-managed timestamps. All fields are optional to support partial updates where members can modify specific profile attributes without requiring complete profile re-submission.

Security considerations ensure that only the member themselves or authorized administrators can modify profile information. Email and password updates require additional verification steps to prevent unauthorized account access. All updates are validated against database constraints and business rules to maintain data integrity.

This DTO integrates with the discussion_board_members table update operations, providing controlled modification of member profile details while maintaining audit trail and security compliance.

member_id.description: Foreign key reference to the member who owns this session. Provides session ownership tracking without exposing detailed member information in session responses.

ip.description: IP address of the member session connection captured during authentication. Used for security auditing, geographic tracking, and connection pattern analysis to detect suspicious activity.

href.description: Connection URL where the member session was established, representing the current page URL at login time. Used for tracking user navigation patterns and session context.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that directed the member to the session, indicating the previous page before authentication. Provides context for user navigation flow and session initiation patterns.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the member session expired or was terminated, null if session remains active. Used for session lifecycle management and automatic cleanup of expired sessions.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the member session was soft deleted, null if session is still active. Supports audit trail preservation while removing active session functionality.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.description:
Authentication session entity for member users tracking connection context and session lifecycle.

Represents individual authentication sessions for registered members, capturing detailed connection information including IP address, access URLs, and session timestamps. Each session belongs to a specific member user and maintains authentication state throughout its lifecycle. Sessions provide the foundation for secure member access to discussion board features including post creation, commenting, and content management.

Sessions are used for security auditing, tracking member activity patterns, and troubleshooting connection issues. The session lifecycle includes creation during authentication, updates for connection changes, expiration for security purposes, and soft deletion for audit trail preservation. Session management ensures secure access control while maintaining comprehensive activity logging for administrative oversight.

This entity integrates with the discussion_board_member_sessions table as defined in the Prisma schema, providing comprehensive session management capabilities for the discussion board platform. The session data supports security compliance, user experience optimization, and administrative monitoring requirements.

id.description: Unique identifier for the member session record.

ip.description: IP address of the member session connection.

href.description: Connection URL where the member session was established.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that directed the member to the session.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the member session was initially created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the member session was last updated.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the member session expired or was terminated.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the member session was soft deleted.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of member session for list operations and efficient data transfer.

Provides essential session information with connection context for display in lists and overview operations. Includes only the most critical fields needed for identification and basic context while maintaining accurate representation of the Prisma schema structure.

This summary type is optimized for performance in list operations, reducing data transfer overhead while providing sufficient information for session identification and connection context. The schema accurately reflects all fields from the discussion_board_member_sessions table as defined in the Prisma schema.

Used primarily in administrative interfaces for session management and audit purposes, providing comprehensive session tracking information without unnecessary data overhead.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts from 1.

limit.description: Number of sessions per page. Maximum limit is 100 sessions per request.

search.description: Search term to filter sessions by IP address, connection URL, or referrer URL.

oneOf.description: Field to sort sessions by. Options include creation date, last update, expiration date, or connection URL.
Field to sort sessions by. Options include creation date, last update, expiration date, or connection URL.

Sorting order for the results. Can be ascending or descending.

order.description: Sorting order for the results. Can be ascending or descending.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for member session queries.

This DTO defines the filtering and pagination options available for searching member authentication sessions. It supports advanced search capabilities including text filtering across multiple session attributes, sorting by various session properties, and configurable pagination.

The search functionality supports filtering by IP address patterns, connection URL matching, referrer URL analysis, and session status indicators. Sorting options include creation date, last update time, expiration date, and connection URL attributes.

Used primarily by administrative interfaces for session management and audit purposes. The parameters allow for efficient retrieval of session records based on connection context, temporal criteria, and session lifecycle status.

ip.description: Updated IP address of the member session connection for tracking connection changes. Captures the current IP address when session details are modified, supporting security auditing and connection tracking.

href.description: Updated connection URL where the member session was established. Records the current page URL when session information is refreshed, providing context for session activity tracking.

referrer.description: Updated referrer URL that directed the member to the session. Tracks the previous page navigation path when session details are modified for analytics and user journey mapping.

expired_at.description: Updated expiration timestamp for the session, allowing session termination or extension. When set to null, indicates the session remains active; when set to a datetime, schedules session expiration at the specified time.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying member session connection details and expiration status.

This DTO allows authorized members to update their own session information, including connection context changes and session expiration settings. All fields are required to ensure complete session tracking integrity and maintain consistent audit trail data.

Security considerations require that only the authenticated member can update their own sessions. The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp when this DTO is applied. Session ownership validation ensures members cannot modify sessions belonging to other users, maintaining strict access control boundaries.

This DTO integrates with the discussion_board_member_sessions table update operations, providing controlled modification of session details while maintaining audit trail and security compliance. Connection tracking fields support security monitoring and user activity analysis.

email.description: Moderator email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all moderators and follows standard email format validation. This field is required for account recovery, system notifications, and serves as the primary contact method for platform communications.

username.description: Moderator username for display and identification. Must be unique across all moderators and serves as the primary handle for moderator recognition within the discussion board platform. Used in URL paths and API operations for moderator-specific actions.

display_name.description: Optional display name for moderator profile customization. Allows moderators to use a different name for public display while maintaining their unique username for authentication purposes. Provides flexibility in how moderators present themselves to the community.

bio.description: Optional biography or description for moderator profile. Provides context about the moderator's role, expertise, or background to help community members understand their moderation approach and build trust through transparency.

moderation_level.description: Moderator privilege level indicating their administrative capabilities. Common levels include basic, senior, and admin, each with progressively broader moderation permissions and responsibilities. Determines access to specific moderation features and content management tools.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.description:
Moderator entity representing administrative users with content management privileges in the discussion board system.

This entity stores comprehensive moderator information including authentication credentials, profile details, and moderation capabilities. Moderators are responsible for maintaining community guidelines, reviewing reported content, removing inappropriate posts/comments, suspending users, and managing discussion categories to ensure platform quality and safety.

The entity supports role-based access control through moderation levels, allowing different privilege tiers for basic moderation tasks versus administrative functions. Profile customization options enable moderators to present themselves appropriately to the community while maintaining professional standards and building trust through transparent communication.

Security considerations include unique email/username constraints, password hashing for authentication, and audit trail tracking through timestamp fields. Soft deletion support allows for account recovery while preserving moderation history and maintaining referential integrity across related entities.

email.description: Updated moderator email address for authentication and communication. Must remain unique across all moderators and follows standard email format validation. This field is optional for partial updates but must be provided when modifying email address.

password.description: Plain text password for moderator authentication updates. Backend will securely hash this password before storage. This field replaces the password_hash field to ensure clients never send pre-hashed passwords.

display_name.description: Optional updated display name for moderator profile customization. Allows moderators to modify their public-facing name while maintaining authentication credentials. Can be omitted if not being modified.

bio.description: Optional updated biography or description for moderator profile. Enables moderators to refresh their profile information to reflect current roles or approaches. Can be omitted if not being modified.

moderation_level.description: Updated moderator privilege level indicating administrative capabilities. Changes to moderation level may require additional authorization checks. Optional for partial updates but required when changing privilege level.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying moderator profile information in the discussion board system.

This DTO supports partial updates to moderator profiles while maintaining data integrity through optional field validation. Unlike creation operations that require all mandatory fields, update operations allow selective modification of specific attributes without requiring complete profile replacement.

Security considerations include authorization verification to ensure only authorized moderators can perform profile updates. The system validates that target moderators exist and are active before applying changes. Profile updates may include changes to display preferences, biographical information, and moderation privileges.

All modifications undergo uniqueness checks for email to prevent conflicts with existing moderator accounts. The operation preserves the moderator's unique identifier and maintains historical timestamps for audit trail purposes while supporting flexible partial updates.

id.description: Primary identifier for the moderator account. This unique UUID serves as the database primary key and ensures each moderator has a distinct identity within the system.

username.description: Moderator username for display and identification. Must be unique across all moderators and serves as the primary handle for moderator recognition within the discussion board platform.

display_name.description: Optional display name for moderator profile customization. Allows moderators to use a different name for public display while maintaining their unique username for authentication purposes.

moderation_level.description: Moderator privilege level indicating their administrative capabilities. Common levels include basic, senior, and admin, each with progressively broader moderation permissions and responsibilities.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created. Records the initial registration date and time for audit trail and account lifecycle tracking.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary.description:
Summary view of moderator information for efficient list displays and assignment tracking.

Provides essential moderator details optimized for quick reference and workflow management. This summary variant excludes sensitive authentication data and detailed profile information to focus on identification, basic profile data, and moderation capabilities.

Used primarily in moderation queue interfaces, assignment tracking systems, and administrative dashboards where detailed moderator profiles are not required but basic identification and capability information is necessary for workflow management.

The summary maintains consistency with the main IDiscussionBoardModerator DTO while optimizing for performance in list operations and reducing data transfer overhead for high-frequency administrative interfaces.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Used for navigating through large result sets efficiently.

limit.description: Number of items per page for pagination. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive to balance performance and usability.

search.description: Search query for filtering moderators by username or email pattern matching. Supports partial matching and case-insensitive search operations.

moderation_level.description: Filter moderators by specific privilege level (e.g., basic, senior, admin). Allows filtering by administrative capabilities and permissions.

oneOf.description: Sort results by moderator username in alphabetical order.
Sort results by moderator email address in alphabetical order.
Sort results by moderation privilege level from basic to admin.
Sort results by account creation date from oldest to newest.
Sort results by last update timestamp from oldest to newest.

sort_by.description: Field to sort the results by. Available options include username, email, moderation level, creation date, and update timestamp.

oneOf.description: Sort results in ascending order (A-Z, oldest first).
Sort results in descending order (Z-A, newest first).

order.description: Sorting order for the results. Can be ascending (asc) or descending (desc).

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving discussion board moderators.

This schema defines the comprehensive query parameters used for searching, filtering, and paginating moderator lists. It supports advanced search capabilities including pattern matching, level-based filtering, and multiple sorting options.

Security considerations include validation of pagination limits to prevent excessive resource consumption and appropriate access controls for moderator information retrieval. The schema ensures that search operations remain performant while providing flexible filtering capabilities for administrative workflows.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderator session record. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format for global uniqueness and security.

discussion_board_moderator_id.description: Foreign key reference to the moderator account that owns this session. Links to the discussion_board_moderators.id field for relationship tracking.

ip.description: IP address of the moderator session connection. Used for security auditing, geographic tracking, and connection context analysis. Captures the source IP where the moderator authenticated.

href.description: Connection URL where the moderator session was established. Records the specific page or endpoint where authentication occurred for audit trail purposes.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that directed the moderator to the session. Useful for tracking navigation patterns and understanding how moderators access the administrative interface.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the moderator session was created. Records the exact moment of authentication and session establishment in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the moderator session was last updated. Tracks session activity and connection changes throughout the session lifecycle.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the moderator session expired or was terminated. Used for session management and automatic cleanup of inactive sessions.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the moderator session was soft deleted. Supports audit trail preservation while marking sessions as inactive for security purposes.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.description:
Authentication sessions for moderator users with administrative privileges.

Tracks moderator login sessions with comprehensive connection context information including IP address, access URLs, and detailed timestamp tracking. Each session belongs to a specific moderator account and maintains authentication state for administrative functions.

Sessions are used for security auditing, access monitoring, and audit trail creation for moderator actions. The session entity supports soft deletion to preserve historical records while maintaining security by marking sessions as inactive.

This entity integrates with the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table as defined in the Prisma schema, maintaining all database relationships and constraints while providing a clean API interface for session management operations.

page.description:
Page number for pagination starting from 1. Used for navigating through large result sets of moderator authentication sessions.

Must be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1. The system will return the requested page of results based on the specified limit.

limit.description:
Number of items per page with a maximum limit of 100 records.

Controls the number of moderator session records returned in a single response. Larger limits improve performance for bulk operations while smaller limits reduce response size for individual queries.

The system enforces a maximum of 100 records per page to prevent excessive resource consumption.

search.description:
Search term to filter sessions by IP address patterns or connection URL content.

Supports partial matching against IP addresses and connection URLs. Useful for finding sessions from specific geographic locations or accessing particular administrative interfaces.

The search applies to both IP address fields and connection URL content using case-insensitive pattern matching.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by specific IP address using exact match.

Useful for security investigations and audit tracing where precise IP address identification is required. Matches the exact IP address stored in the session record.

Must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address format. Supports filtering for sessions originating from specific network locations.

created_at_start.description:
Filter sessions created after this timestamp using ISO 8601 format.

Useful for time-based filtering to find recent sessions or sessions within specific date ranges. The timestamp must be in UTC format.

Example: "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z" would filter sessions created after January 15, 2024 at 10:30 AM UTC.

created_at_end.description:
Filter sessions created before this timestamp using ISO 8601 format.

Used in combination with created_at_start to define date ranges for session retrieval. The timestamp must be in UTC format.

Example: "2024-01-20T18:45:00Z" would filter sessions created before January 20, 2024 at 6:45 PM UTC.

expired.description:
Filter by session expiration status to identify active or terminated sessions.

When set to true, returns only sessions that have expired or been terminated. When set to false, returns only active sessions.

Useful for session management and security monitoring to identify sessions requiring attention or cleanup.

oneOf.description: Sort results by session creation timestamp in ascending or descending order.
Sort results by session last update timestamp for recent activity tracking.
Sort results by session expiration timestamp for expiration management.
Sort results by IP address for geographic or network-based organization.

sort_by.description:
Field selection for sorting moderator session results.

Determines which session attribute is used for ordering the returned results. Supports sorting by creation time, last update time, expiration status, or IP address.

Each sorting option provides different organizational benefits for session management and audit analysis.

oneOf.description: Ascending sort order from oldest to newest or lowest to highest values.
Descending sort order from newest to oldest or highest to lowest values.

order.description:
Sort direction specification for organizing session results.

Controls whether results are displayed in ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first) order based on the selected sort_by field.

Ascending order is typically used for chronological analysis while descending order is useful for recent activity review.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.IReques.description:
Comprehensive search and filtering parameters for retrieving moderator authentication sessions.

Provides advanced filtering capabilities for moderator session queries including pagination controls, search functionality, IP address filtering, date range selection, and expiration status filtering. Supports complex query patterns for security monitoring and access control analysis.

Used by administrative interfaces to search and audit moderator session activity across the discussion board platform. The operation integrates with the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating all available session fields and relationships.

Security considerations include appropriate filtering of session information based on the requesting moderator's authorization level. Only authenticated moderators can access session information, with session data being filtered to show only sessions belonging to the specified moderator.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the moderator session generated automatically using UUID v4.

Primary key field that uniquely identifies each moderator authentication session record in the system. Used for session tracking, audit logging, and administrative operations.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness and prevents collision across distributed systems.

ip.description:
IP address of the moderator session connection captured during authentication.

Records the network location from which the moderator accessed the system. Used for security monitoring, geographic analysis, and access pattern tracking.

Essential for audit tracing and security incident investigation to identify session origins and potential unauthorized access attempts.

href.description:
Connection URL where the moderator session was established during login.

Captures the specific administrative interface or dashboard URL accessed by the moderator. Useful for understanding moderator workflow patterns and interface usage.

Provides context for session establishment and helps identify which administrative functions were accessed during the session.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that directed the moderator to the session establishment point.

Records the navigation path that led the moderator to the authentication interface. Useful for understanding moderator access patterns and workflow navigation.

Helps identify common entry points and navigation patterns for moderator administrative activities.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator session was created and authentication established.

Records the exact moment when the moderator successfully authenticated and the session became active. Used for session lifecycle tracking and activity timeline analysis.

Essential for audit purposes and session duration calculation across the moderation workflow.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator session was last updated with new connection details.

Tracks the most recent activity within the session, including page navigation, action execution, or connection parameter changes. Useful for session activity monitoring.

Helps identify active sessions and recent moderator activity for security and workflow management.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator session expired or was manually terminated.

Records the end of the session lifecycle, either through automatic expiration based on timeout settings or manual termination by the moderator or administrator.

Essential for session duration analysis, security compliance, and inactive session cleanup operations.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.ISummar.description:
Summary view of discussion board moderator authentication sessions for efficient listing and reference.

Provides essential information about moderator login sessions including connection context and timestamps while maintaining performance for administrative interfaces. This summary excludes moderator foreign key and soft-delete flags for security compliance.

Moderator sessions track authentication state and connection metadata for audit tracing of administrative actions. Each session belongs to a specific moderator user and maintains access to administrative functions including content moderation, user management, and system configuration.

The summary view is optimized for session listing operations in administrative dashboards and audit interfaces where detailed session information is required but full object loading would impact performance. Field selection focuses on essential session attributes needed for security monitoring and access control analysis while protecting authentication context and internal system flags.

Session records include comprehensive connection metadata captured during authentication, supporting detailed audit trails and security incident investigation. The foreign key relationship to moderators is maintained server-side for authorization verification but not exposed in the response DTO for security reasons.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator session expired or was terminated. Can be updated to extend or shorten session validity. Administrators can modify this field to manage session lifecycle and access control.

This field allows administrative control over session duration without compromising security. The expiration time can be adjusted for legitimate purposes such as extending session validity for ongoing administrative tasks or shortening it for security reasons.

Security considerations require that only the expiration time can be modified, while connection context fields (IP, URL, referrer) remain immutable to preserve audit trail integrity.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.IUpdate.description:
Update data for moderator session properties allowing modification of expiration time only.

This DTO defines the mutable fields that administrators can update for existing moderator authentication sessions. Only the expiration time field is included as it represents legitimate administrative control over session duration.

Security considerations require that connection context fields (IP, URL, referrer) are excluded from client modification to preserve audit trail integrity. These fields are automatically managed by the server based on actual connection context and cannot be manipulated by clients.

The update operation validates that session modifications comply with security policies and audit requirements. All modifications are logged for compliance and security monitoring purposes.

title.description:
Post title summarizing the discussion topic. Must be between 5 and 200 characters to ensure meaningful content while preventing excessively long titles. Titles should clearly indicate the post's subject matter for effective content discovery.

Title validation ensures posts have descriptive headings that help users understand the discussion focus. The character limits balance readability with content discovery requirements.

content.description:
Main content body of the post supporting Markdown formatting. Must be between 50 and 10,000 characters to ensure substantive content while maintaining reasonable post length. Supports rich formatting for enhanced readability and engagement.

Content validation prevents spam posts while allowing meaningful discussion. The character limits ensure posts contain sufficient substance without becoming excessively long.

discussion_board_channel_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the discussion board channel where this post belongs. Required for proper content categorization and organizational structure.

This field represents a legitimate selection of content categorization, not authentication context. Users choose which channel their post belongs to based on topic relevance.

discussion_board_section_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the discussion board section within the selected channel. Provides finer content organization within broader channel categories.

Like channel selection, section selection represents legitimate content categorization that users can choose based on topic specificity.

IDiscussionBoardPost.ICreate.description:
Creation data for a new discussion board post including content, title, and channel/section categorization.

This DTO defines the required fields when creating a new discussion post on the economic/political discussion board. The post is initially created in draft status with system-managed defaults for timestamps, pinning status, and locking state.

Security considerations require that authentication context fields are excluded from the request body as they are automatically populated from authenticated user context. The system validates content against spam prevention and community guidelines before publication.

Channel and section categorization fields represent legitimate user selections for content organization, not authentication context manipulation.

title.description: Post title summarizing the discussion topic. Must be between 5 and 200 characters.

content.description: Main content body of the post supporting Markdown formatting. Must be between 50 and 10,000 characters.

status.description: Current status of the post: draft, published, archived, or deleted.

is_pinned.description: Whether the post is pinned to the top of the discussion board.

is_locked.description: Whether the post is locked from further comments.

channel_code.description: Unique channel code for categorization. References discussion_board_channels.name

section_code.description: Unique section code within the channel. References discussion_board_sections.name

IDiscussionBoardPost.IUpdate.description:
Update data for an existing discussion board post.

This schema defines the fields that can be modified when updating an existing discussion post. All fields are optional to support partial updates.

Foreign key references use unique code fields (channel_code, section_code) instead of UUID IDs for better readability and consistency with API patterns. Security considerations ensure that ownership fields and system-managed timestamps cannot be modified through the update operation.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the comment.

content.description: Comment text content with Markdown formatting support. Validated for length between 1 and 2000 characters as per requirements.

status.description: Current comment status: 'draft', 'published', 'deleted'. Controls comment visibility and management.

thread_level.description: Nesting level of comment in thread hierarchy. Root comments have level 0, replies increment by 1. Limited to maximum 3 levels deep.

created_at.description: Timestamp when comment was initially created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when comment was last modified.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when comment was soft deleted. Null if comment is active.

post.description: Reference to the parent post containing this comment.

author.description: Reference to the member who authored this comment.

parent_id.description: Reference to parent comment for threaded replies. Null if this is a root comment.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Threaded comments on discussion board posts with support for attachments and moderation.

Stores user comments on discussion posts with hierarchical threading capabilities. Each comment belongs to a specific post and can have parent comments for threaded discussions. Comments support attachment uploads and have their own lifecycle independent from posts.

Comments require member authentication and can be moderated separately from posts. The system maintains comment threading up to 3 levels deep as specified in requirements. Comments have their own validation rules and management workflows distinct from post content.

Comment lifecycle includes creation, editing within time limits, and soft deletion. The system tracks comment status and maintains audit trails for moderation purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the comment.

content.description: Comment text content with Markdown formatting support. Validated for length between 1 and 2000 characters as per requirements.

status.description: Current comment status: 'draft', 'published', 'deleted'. Controls comment visibility and management.

thread_level.description: Nesting level of comment in thread hierarchy. Root comments have level 0, replies increment by 1. Limited to maximum 3 levels deep.

post.description: Parent post information providing context for where this comment belongs.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of discussion board comments for list displays.

Provides essential comment information including content preview, status, creation timestamp, and contextual references to author and parent post. Designed for efficient display in comment lists and thread overviews.

Includes transformed relation objects for author and post to provide complete contextual information without requiring additional API calls. Excludes detailed relations and large text fields to maintain performance in list views.

Suitable for displaying multiple comments simultaneously with complete contextual information about authorship and post context.

content.description: Comment text content with Markdown formatting support. Validated for length between 1 and 2000 characters as per requirements.

parent_id.description: Reference to parent comment for threaded replies. Null if this is a root comment.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new comment on a discussion board post.

This DTO includes the essential information needed to create a comment, including the content text and optional parent comment reference for threaded replies. The comment author and parent post identifiers are provided through authentication context and path parameters respectively.

The content field supports Markdown formatting and is validated for length requirements (1-2000 characters). When parent_id is provided, the system automatically calculates the appropriate thread level based on the parent comment's nesting depth, ensuring compliance with the maximum 3-level threading requirement.

System-managed fields such as id, status, timestamps, and author/post relationships are automatically populated by the backend and should not be included in the request body.

content.description: Updated comment text content with Markdown formatting support. Validated for length between 1 and 2000 characters as per requirements.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Data required to update an existing comment on a discussion board post.

This DTO allows authenticated members to modify the content of their comments within the allowed timeframe. Only the content field can be updated - all other fields including relationships, status, and timestamps are managed by the system.

The operation validates that the comment exists, belongs to the specified post, and that the requesting member is the original author of the comment. Comment updates are subject to time-based restrictions as specified in requirements.

System-managed fields such as id, status, timestamps, and relationships cannot be modified through this DTO. The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed by the backend to track modification history.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts from 1.

limit.description: Number of comments per page. Maximum 100 comments per request.

search.description: Search term to filter comments by content.

status.description: Filter comments by status: 'draft', 'published', 'deleted'.

thread_level.description: Filter comments by thread nesting level (0-3).

author_id.description: Filter comments by specific author member ID.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating discussion board comments.

This DTO defines the search and filter criteria for retrieving comments from the discussion board. It supports pagination, content search, status filtering, thread level filtering, author filtering, and sorting options.

The search parameter performs full-text search on comment content. Status filtering allows retrieving comments by their current lifecycle state. Thread level filtering enables retrieving comments at specific nesting depths within threaded discussions. Author filtering allows retrieving comments by specific members.

Pagination parameters ensure efficient retrieval of large comment datasets. Sorting options allow ordering comments by creation or modification timestamps in ascending or descending order.

IDiscussionBoardPostAttachment.description:
File attachments associated with discussion board posts.

Stores metadata for files uploaded by members to support their posts with additional evidence, research materials, or visual content. Each attachment is specifically linked to a single post and maintains its own lifecycle separate from the post content.

Attachments undergo security scanning and validation before being made available for download. The system tracks upload status, file properties, and access patterns to ensure proper attachment management.

Supports various file types including images (JPG, PNG, GIF) and documents (PDF, DOC, DOCX) with size limitations enforced during upload.

This request schema provides comprehensive search capabilities for attachments associated with discussion board comments. It supports filtering by file properties, upload status, security scan results, and date ranges.

Creation DTO for discussion board comment attachments.

Contains the metadata required to create a new file attachment for a comment. This DTO is used when members upload files to support their discussion contributions.

The creation process validates file properties against platform restrictions, including size limits and allowed file types. Security scanning is initiated after basic validation passes to ensure file safety.

Note that the parent comment ID and member information are provided through authentication context and path parameters, not included in this DTO. The upload status defaults to 'pending' and security scan result defaults to 'pending' during initial creation.

IDiscussionBoardContentReport.description:
Main entity for content reports with shared attributes and actor type classification.

Serves as the central repository for all content reports submitted on the discussion board. Contains common fields shared across all report types regardless of which actor (member or moderator) created them.

The actor field provides complete context about the reporter with summary information, enabling efficient filtering and relationship management. This design follows proper normalization while providing rich context for moderation workflows.

Reports can target various content types including posts, comments, and member profiles, with each report maintaining its own lifecycle and moderation workflow state.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the content report. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format upon report creation.

Serves as the primary key for report identification and reference in the moderation workflow. Essential for tracking individual reports throughout their lifecycle from submission to resolution.

actor.description:
Actor who created the content report. Provides complete context about the reporter including actor type (member or moderator) and identification information.

The actor reference enables moderators to understand who submitted the report, which is crucial for assessing report credibility and context. Actor information helps in identifying patterns and potential misuse of the reporting system.

content.description:
Content being reported. Provides context about the target of the report including content type (post, comment, or member profile) and identification.

Essential for moderators to quickly identify and access the reported content for review. The content reference enables efficient navigation to the problematic material while maintaining separation of concerns between reporting and content entities.

report_reason.description:
Reason category for the content report. Common values include: 'spam', 'harassment', 'inappropriate', 'misinformation', 'copyright', 'other'.

Categorizes the nature of the reported violation, helping moderators prioritize and route reports appropriately. Each reason category may have different handling procedures and response times based on platform policies and severity levels.

status.description:
Current status of the report in the moderation workflow. Valid values: 'pending', 'under_review', 'resolved', 'dismissed', 'escalated'.

Tracks the progress of each report through the moderation pipeline. Status changes reflect actions taken by moderators and help manage workflow efficiency. The status field enables filtering and prioritization of moderation tasks.

priority.description:
Priority level assigned for moderation handling. Values: 'low', 'normal', 'high', 'critical'. Priority is assigned based on report severity, content sensitivity, and potential impact.

Helps moderators triage reports effectively, ensuring urgent matters receive prompt attention. Priority assignment may be automated based on report characteristics or manually adjusted by moderators based on context.

report_details.description:
Detailed explanation provided by the reporter explaining why the content should be moderated. Contains the specific concerns, context, and rationale behind the report submission.

Essential for understanding the reporter's perspective and the nature of the reported violation. The details field provides moderators with the necessary context to make informed decisions about content moderation actions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the content report was initially submitted to the moderation system. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format for standardization.

Provides chronological context for report handling and helps identify reporting patterns over time. The creation timestamp is also used for filtering reports by date ranges in moderation interfaces.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the content report was last updated with new status, priority changes, or moderation actions. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

Essential for tracking moderation workflow progress and identifying stale reports that may require follow-up. The update timestamp helps moderators monitor their response times and workflow efficiency.

IDiscussionBoardContentReport.ISummary.description:
Summary view of content reports designed for efficient listing and overview displays in moderation interfaces.

Provides complete information for moderation queues and report dashboards, including transformed foreign key relations to actors and content for immediate context. This summary variant excludes large text fields and detailed metadata to optimize performance in list operations.

The schema maintains essential report information while supporting quick scanning and filtering capabilities required by moderators. It serves as the primary data structure for report listing operations, search results, and moderation dashboard displays.

Optimized for performance in moderation interfaces where quick scanning and filtering of reports is required while maintaining complete relation context. The summary structure balances information density with response performance to support efficient moderation workflows.

page.description:
Page number for pagination using 1-based indexing. Required parameter for controlling result pagination.

Determines which set of results to retrieve from the paginated dataset. Page numbers start at 1, and the system returns the specified page of results based on the limit parameter.

limit.description:
Number of content report records to return per page. Controls the size of each paginated result set.

Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Lower values improve response performance for large datasets, while higher values reduce the number of pagination requests needed to retrieve complete result sets.

status.description:
Filter content reports by their current moderation status. Valid values: 'pending', 'under_review', 'resolved', 'dismissed', 'escalated'.

Allows moderators to focus on reports in specific workflow states. For example, filtering by 'pending' shows only new reports awaiting initial review, while 'under_review' shows reports currently being processed.

priority.description:
Filter content reports by their assigned priority level. Valid values: 'low', 'normal', 'high', 'critical'.

Enables prioritization of moderation tasks by focusing on higher-priority reports first. Critical priority reports typically require immediate attention due to their potential impact on platform safety.

actor_type.description:
Filter content reports by the type of actor who submitted them. Valid values: 'member', 'moderator'.

Helps identify reporting patterns based on actor types. Member reports typically represent community concerns, while moderator reports may indicate systematic content issues requiring administrative attention.

report_reason.description:
Filter content reports by their reason category. Common values: 'spam', 'harassment', 'inappropriate', 'misinformation', 'copyright', 'other'.

Enables focused moderation on specific types of content violations. Different reason categories may require different expertise or handling procedures from the moderation team.

content_type.description:
Filter content reports by the type of content being reported. Valid values: 'post', 'comment', 'member_profile'.

Allows moderators to specialize their review based on content types. Each content type may have different moderation guidelines and handling requirements based on platform policies.

content_id.description:
Filter content reports by a specific content identifier using UUID format.

Useful for finding all reports targeting a particular piece of content, which can help identify patterns of reporting or repeated issues with specific content items.

created_at_start.description:
Filter content reports created after this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

Enables time-based filtering to focus on recent reports or specific reporting periods. Combined with created_at_end, creates a date range filter for chronological report analysis.

created_at_end.description:
Filter content reports created before this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

Complements created_at_start to define complete date ranges for report filtering. Essential for historical analysis and reporting period comparisons.

search.description:
Text search within the report_details field of content reports. Supports basic text matching for finding reports containing specific keywords or phrases.

Enables moderators to search for reports based on textual content within the reporter's explanation. Useful for identifying patterns, specific issues, or recurring concerns mentioned across multiple reports.

The actor_type field has been removed as it will be automatically set to 'member' based on the authenticated user's role. This ensures proper report categorization and routing to the appropriate moderation workflows while maintaining security by preventing client-side actor identity manipulation.

This schema maintains proper separation between user-provided data and system-managed fields, ensuring that reporters can submit comprehensive reports while the backend handles technical details like timestamps, identifiers, actor classification, and audit trails automatically.
